title: Tülu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
data_curation: Tülu 3 targets seven core skills (knowledge recall, reasoning, math, coding, instruction following, chat, safety). Prompts come from public datasets — WildChat, OpenAssistant, No Robots, FLAN v2, UltraFeedback, OpenMathInstruct 2, NuminaMath-TIR, Evol-CodeAlpaca, Aya, SciRIFF, TableGPT — plus large-scale persona-driven synthetic generation (Chan et al. 2024) using ~250K personas from Persona Hub, with GPT-4o writing problems/solutions and Claude-3.5-Sonnet for code. This yields ~939K SFT samples, ~354K preference pairs (271K for 8B, 334K for 70B), and ~30K verifiable RLVR prompts (GSM8K 7,473; MATH 7,500; IFEval 14,973). Preference data combines on-policy Tülu-3-SFT generations with off-policy responses from a 22-model pool, judged by GPT-4o (1–5 across helpfulness, instruction following, honesty, truthfulness) then binarized. All prompts are decontaminated against the eval suite via 8-gram matching (>50% token overlap); datasets with >2% overlap are removed or filtered.
curriculum: A four-stage recipe applied to Llama 3.1 base models (8B, 70B, 405B), each stage resuming from the prior checkpoint: (1) data curation, (2) supervised fine-tuning, (3) preference tuning with length-normalized DPO, (4) RLVR with PPO. SFT uses 2 epochs, a sum loss (token-equal weighting to fix loss-aggregation bugs), LR 5e-6 (8B) / 2e-6 (70B), effective batch 128, max length 4096. DPO runs 1 epoch at LR 5e-7 (8B) / 2e-7 (70B), β=5, length 2048. RLVR is applied last, sweeping KL coefficient β∈[0.1,0.01] (final 8B β=0.05, 70B β=0.07). At 405B, GSM8K was dropped from RLVR (saturated) and only MATH was used. Cross-stage data is mixed deliberately: skill-specific SFT data, then on+off-policy preferences, then verifiable prompts. Online DPO and rejection-sampling self-play were tried but did not help and were dropped.
method: The headline contribution is RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards): the standard KL-constrained RLHF objective is kept but the learned reward model is replaced by a deterministic verifier v(x,y), giving max E[v(x,y) − β·KL(πθ‖πref)], with v=α (=10) if the answer is verified correct and 0 otherwise. It is optimized with PPO on math (exact-match answer extraction) and verifiable instruction following (constraint checkers). Key implementation choices: value model initialized from a general RM (UltraFeedback-trained, EOS-token reward), dropout disabled for consistent log-probs, non-EOS penalty of −10, advantage whitening, and multi-epoch training with shuffled prompts. Preference tuning uses length-normalized DPO (DPO with length-normalized log-probs, à la SimPO), chosen over SimPO, vanilla DPO, and PPO. Infrastructure uses ZeRO-3 plus asynchronous RL with vLLM/PagedAttention inference on dedicated Ray-allocated GPUs, scaling PPO to 405B (with an 8B value model).
eval_metrics: Evaluation uses Tülu 3 Eval, released via the OLMES toolkit, split into development and unseen sets. Development: MMLU (0-shot CoT), PopQA (15-shot), TruthfulQA (MC2), BigBenchHard (3-shot CoT), DROP (F1), MATH (4-shot flex EM), GSM8K (8-shot EM), HumanEval/HumanEval+ (pass@10), IFEval (prompt-loose pass@1), AlpacaEval 2 (length-controlled winrate), and a 6-task safety average (XSTest, HarmBench, DAN, JailbreakTrigger, WildJailbreakTest, WildGuardTest). Unseen: MMLU-Pro, GPQA, AGIEval-English, Deepmind Mathematics, BigCodeBench, IFEval-OOD, HREF. Headline: Tülu 3 70B averages 76.2, beating Llama 3.1 70B Instruct (74.1), GPT-4o-mini (69.6), and Claude 3.5 Haiku (75.3); Tülu 3 405B reaches 80.7 (w/ safety), competitive with GPT-4o (81.6). RLVR lifts 8B GSM8K 84.3→87.6, MATH 42.0→43.7, IFEval 81.1→82.4.
key_results: Tülu 3 70B averages 76.2 on Tülu 3 Eval, surpassing Llama 3.1 70B Instruct (74.1), GPT-4o-mini (69.6), and Claude 3.5 Haiku (75.3). RLVR improves the 8B model on GSM8K (84.3→87.6), MATH (42.0→43.7), and IFEval (81.1→82.4). Tülu 3 405B reaches 80.7 avg (with safety), competitive with GPT-4o (81.6) and DeepSeek-V3 (75.9).
evolution_note: Tülu 3 extends the open post-training line of Tülu 2/Zephyr-β toward closed-style multi-stage recipes (cf. Llama 3.1), borrowing persona-driven synthetic data, DPO/SimPO, and PPO/RLHF, and formalizing verifiable-reward RL (cf. STaR/VinePPO) as RLVR. Its fully open data/recipe and RLVR stage anticipate the 2024–25 wave of RL-with-verifiable-rewards methods (e.g., GRPO, DeepSeek-R1) and reproducible open post-training.
